messages.content:
Good news — this project is already very well-prepared for release. I found:

- **`meridian-extension/`** — the packaged candidate directory (validated, 49 files)
- **`RELEASE_VALIDATION.md`** — a full release validation record: **Pass, v1.1.0 is release-ready**, tests green (126/126), archive/directory hashes verified, headed Chrome 150 smoke test clean
- **`STORE_LISTING.md`** — complete draft copy for the Chrome Web Store dashboard (listing text, privacy practices, permission justifications, data handling disclosure)
- **`PRIVACY.md`** — privacy policy source
- **`store-assets/`** — a promo tile image (440×280) + README

So the code/QA work is essentially done. What's left is **owner-only Chrome Web Store dashboard work** that no agent can do on your behalf (it requires your Google account / developer console access). Per `RELEASE_VALIDATION.md` §5/§6, the outstanding items are:

1. **Package the exact validated candidate** — zip up `meridian-extension/` (candidate directory tree SHA-256 `5702e8ce…`) and confirm it matches after re-extracting, before uploading.
2. **Publish/repair the privacy policy URL** (`https://emberstone-studio.com/docs/privacy/`) — currently generic boilerplate; needs Meridian-specific additions (screenshot capture, meta/H1/H2 extraction, tab/browsing-activity collection, `chrome.storage.sync` behavior, retention language) per `STORE_LISTING.md` §2.4.
3. **Log into the Chrome Web Store Developer Dashboard** and paste in the pre-written copy from `STORE_LISTING.md`: listing text, single-purpose description, data-type declarations, the three data-usage certifications, and each permission justification.
4. **Upload store assets** — you have the promo tile; check if you still need screenshots/icon per the dashboard's requirements (`store-assets/README.md` may note what's missing).
5. **Submit for review.**

Want me to:
- **(a)** Have the Coder build the release ZIP from `meridian-extension/` right now and verify its hash against the validated `5702e8ce…` tree hash, so you have an upload-ready artifact, and/or
- **(b)** Have the Writer draft the revised, Meridian-specific privacy policy text to replace the generic boilerplate at the emberstone-studio.com URL?

The actual dashboard submission (steps 3, 5) will need to happen in your browser since it requires your Google account.

50	# Meridian — Chrome Web Store submission copy
51	
52	Last updated: July 26, 2026
53	
54	Publisher-facing copy for the Chrome Web Store listing, the **Privacy
55	practices** tab, and the per-permission justification fields. It is derived from
56	the source in this repository (manifest, `background.js`, `utils/`, and
57	`components/`) and reconciled with `PRIVACY.md` and `README.md`.
58	
59	> **Owner action required.** Everything here is draft copy for review. It is not
60	> a submission and does not certify anything in the Chrome Web Store dashboard.
61	> Paste each block into the matching dashboard field, confirm it against the
62	> exact archive you upload, and complete the owner-only follow-ups at the end of
63	> this document. Items marked **[OWNER-ONLY — NOT DONE]** were not and cannot be
64	> performed from the repository.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## 1. Store listing
69	
70	### Name
71	Meridian
72	
73	### Summary (short description, ≤132 characters)
74	Spatial tab command center — a visual new-tab page that turns your open tabs
75	into searchable thumbnail cards.
76	
77	### Category (suggested)
78	Workflow & Planning (or Productivity)
79	
80	### Detailed description
81	Meridian replaces your new-tab page with a spatial command center for your open
82	tabs.
83	
84	Your tabs appear as live thumbnail cards, organized into workspace lanes that
85	map to Chrome tab groups or to custom groups you create in Meridian. Drag to
86	reorder tabs within and across groups, collapse lanes you are not using, and
87	hover a card to open a full-size preview with the tab's title and URL.
88	
89	**Features**
90	- **Tab cards & workspace lanes** — every open tab as a live thumbnail, grouped
91	  into collapsible lanes with drag-and-drop reordering.
92	- **Local search** — instantly find open tabs by title, URL, domain, and page
93	  context. Bookmark and history search are optional and off until you turn them
94	  on.
95	- **Multi-engine web search** — search with Google, DuckDuckGo, Bing, or Brave
96	  from the top of every new-tab page; your choice is remembered.
97	- **Theming & backgrounds** — Light, Dark, or System theme; solid colors,
98	  gradient presets, curated Picsum photos, or your own uploaded image.
99	- **Tab organization** — optionally cluster ungrouped tabs by domain.
100	- **Flexible new-tab behavior** — open a fresh Meridian view, return to a pinned
101	  Meridian tab, or load a custom homepage.
102	- **Keyboard-first** — jump to Meridian, move between tabs and lanes, focus
103	  search, and create groups without the mouse.
104	
105	**Privacy**
106	Meridian runs entirely in your browser. It has no accounts, no analytics, and no
107	Meridian-operated server. Your tab, page, screenshot, bookmark, and history data
108	stays in your Chrome profile. Full details are in the extension's privacy policy.
109	
110	---
111	
112	## 2. Privacy practices tab
113	
114	### 2.1 Single purpose (single-purpose description field)
115	Meridian is a new-tab replacement that helps users view, search, and organize
116	their open browser tabs as a visual, spatial workspace. Every permission and
117	data access exists to render tabs as searchable thumbnail cards, to search local
118	browser data the user opts into, and to personalize the new-tab surface.
119	
120	### 2.2 Data types collected or used
121	Declare the following categories in the dashboard. All are used **on-device for
122	the extension's features**; none are transferred to a Meridian-operated server.
123	
124	| Dashboard data type | Applies? | What it covers in Meridian |
125	| --- | --- | --- |
126	| **Web browsing activity** | Yes | Open tab titles, URLs, domains, tab-group membership, window IDs, tab activation/previous-tab state, and — only if the user enables them — bookmark and browsing-history entries used for local search. |
127	| **Website content** | Yes | Per-tab meta-description and H1/H2 heading text read after a page finishes loading, and JPEG screenshots of the visible area of active tabs captured for thumbnails/previews. Screenshots can contain whatever is on screen at capture time. |
128	| **User activity** | Yes (recommended) | Tab activation, previous-tab tracking, grouping, ordering, and workspace assignments that drive the UI. Disclosed here because reviewers may treat this interaction/usage state as user-activity data. |
129	| Personally identifiable information | No | Not collected. |
130	| Health information | No | Not collected. |
131	| Financial and payment information | No | Not collected. |
132	| Authentication information | No | Not collected. |
133	| Personal communications | No | Not collected. |
134	| Location | No | Not collected. |
135	
136	> The user's **uploaded custom background image** and **preferences** (theme,
137	> background choice, search provider, enabled local-search sources, new-tab
138	> behavior, optional homepage URL, domain-grouping) are user-provided content
139	> stored on the device. Preferences sync through the user's own Chrome Sync if
140	> enabled; the uploaded image bytes and captured screenshots are never placed in
141	> sync storage. Map these to the dashboard's user-content categories as the
142	> current form requires.
143	
144	### 2.3 Data usage certifications
145	Based on the reviewed source, the publisher should be able to affirm all three
146	required certifications — **confirm each against the uploaded archive before
147	checking the box:**
148	
149	- ☑ I do **not** sell or transfer user data to third parties outside of the
150	  approved use cases.
151	- ☑ I do **not** use or transfer user data for purposes unrelated to my item's
152	  single purpose.
153	- ☑ I do **not** use or transfer user data to determine creditworthiness or for
154	  lending purposes.
155	
156	### 2.4 Privacy policy URL
157	`https://emberstone-studio.com/docs/privacy/`
158	
159	This is a catch-all Emberstone Studio policy, not Meridian-specific text, and it
160	is not yet a reliable substitute for `PRIVACY.md`'s Meridian-specific
161	disclosures (see the accuracy gaps below). **[OWNER ACTION STILL NEEDED]**
162	Before entering this URL in the dashboard, add explicit, product-level coverage
163	of: automatic visible-tab screenshot capture, automatic per-page
164	meta-description/H1/H2 extraction, automatic tab/browsing-activity collection,
165	that `chrome.storage.sync` preference data can sync across the user's own
166	signed-in devices (not device-local-only), and that Meridian's stored data is
167	retained persistently until eviction/tab-close/manual-clear rather than
168	"session data [that] deletes automatically." Confirm the final published text
169	against `PRIVACY.md` once revised.
170	
171	---
172	
173	## 3. Data handling disclosure (paste-ready listing block)
174	
175	Meridian processes the following **locally in your browser** to provide its
176	features. Most of it stays in on-device storage; preferences are the exception
177	and can sync through your own Chrome Sync account (see "Local & sync storage"
178	below):
179	
180	- **Browsing activity** — open tab titles, URLs, domains, tab-group membership,
181	  and tab activation/order, used to display, search, and manage your tabs. A
182	  local search index and workspace/UI state are stored in `chrome.storage.local`.
183	- **Website content** — after a page loads, Meridian reads its meta description
184	  and H1/H2 headings so local search can match page context beyond the title and
185	  URL. It does not read form input or other page-body text.
186	- **Screenshots** — Meridian captures the visible area of active tabs after tab
187	  activation or page load, and during a user-requested full refresh that cycles
188	  eligible tabs. Automatic captures (activation/page load) do not filter by URL
189	  in Meridian's code — Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` API itself refuses
190	  `chrome://`, Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so only those
191	  attempts fail; any other page, including one with sensitive content on
192	  screen, is captured. The full refresh additionally skips `chrome://`,
193	  `chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's own code before
194	  switching to them. Screenshots are stored as JPEG blobs in extension-local
195	  IndexedDB; cache metadata and refresh markers use `chrome.storage.local`.
196	  Storage targets roughly 200 entries / ~50 MB and
197	  prunes the oldest thumbnails first, but a still-open tab's thumbnail is never
198	  evicted to make room, so usage can exceed that target while those tabs stay
199	  open. A tab's thumbnail is removed when the tab closes.
200	- **Local & sync storage** — preferences (theme, background, search provider,
201	  enabled local-search sources, new-tab behavior, optional homepage, domain
202	  grouping) are stored in `chrome.storage.sync`. If the user has Chrome Sync
203	  turned on, Chrome syncs this data through the user's own Google/Chrome
204	  account to their other signed-in devices, subject to the user's Chrome Sync
205	  settings — it is not Meridian-operated syncing. Workspaces, search metadata,
206	  thumbnails, the Meridian/previous tab IDs, and an uploaded custom background
207	  image stay in `chrome.storage.local` / IndexedDB and are not synced.
208	- **Optional bookmarks & history** — off by default. Meridian requests bookmark
209	  or history access only when you enable that source in Settings → Local Search
210	  or select its search scope, and queries it only to show local-search results.
211	  It keeps no separate persistent copy; revoking access turns the source off.
212	- **External requests** — search-provider icons load from fixed Google,
213	  DuckDuckGo, Bing, and Brave icon URLs (these contain no visited URL); favicons
214	  resolve through Chrome's packaged `_favicon` provider (not Google S2); the
215	  background settings load photo previews and selected photos from
216	  `picsum.photos` by seed. Starting a web search, opening a result, or choosing a
217	  custom homepage navigates your browser to that destination normally.
218	- **Retention & deletion** — data persists in local/sync storage until replaced,
219	  evicted, cleared, or removed with the extension or profile. Closing a tab
220	  deletes its cached thumbnail and search entry (including extracted metadata).
221	  You can clear all extension data through Chrome's controls.
222	- **Outbound links in Settings** — the Settings panel's Emberstone Studio
223	  footer contains two static links: the studio site
224	  (`https://emberstone-studio.com`) and a Ko-fi donation page
225	  (`https://ko-fi.com/emberstonestudio`). They do nothing until the user
226	  explicitly clicks one, which opens that destination in a new tab. Meridian
227	  makes no background request for them and adds no click tracking or analytics.
228	- **No telemetry or backend** — Meridian has no Meridian-operated server, no
229	  analytics or advertising SDK, no account system, and no telemetry uploader.
230	
231	---
232	
233	## 4. Permission justifications
234	
235	Paste each string into the matching "why do you need this permission?" field.
236	
237	### Required permissions
238	
239	**`tabs`**
240	Read tab titles, URLs, domains, and group/window membership and act on tabs
241	(activate, close, move, group, restore) so Meridian can render the new-tab page's
242	tab cards, power local tab search, and manage tabs from its UI.
243	
244	**`tabGroups`**
245	Read and manage Chrome tab groups so Meridian's workspace lanes reflect and can
246	modify tab-group membership and grouping.
247	
248	**`storage`**
249	Persist the user's preferences, workspaces, tab-search index (including extracted
250	page metadata), thumbnail cache metadata, and tab-tracking state in
251	`chrome.storage.local`/`chrome.storage.sync`, plus JPEG thumbnail blobs in
252	IndexedDB, so settings and layout survive across sessions.
253	
254	**`unlimitedStorage`**
255	Screenshot thumbnails are stored as JPEG blobs in IndexedDB and can exceed the
256	default storage quota. `unlimitedStorage` lets the local thumbnail cache hold enough
257	entries to be useful. Code targets roughly 200 entries / ~50 MB and prunes the
258	oldest thumbnails first when over that target, but never evicts a thumbnail for
259	a tab that is still open — so actual usage can exceed the target while those
260	tabs stay open.
261	
262	**`favicon`**
263	Display site icons for tabs and search results by resolving page URLs through
264	Chrome's packaged `_favicon` provider, avoiding third-party favicon lookups.
265	
266	**`sidePanel`**
267	Provide Meridian's side-panel UI, which opens when the toolbar icon is clicked.
268	
269	**`scripting`**
270	After an open tab finishes loading, run a one-shot extractor that reads only that
271	page's meta description and H1/H2 heading text into the local tab-search index,
272	so local search can match page context beyond the title and URL. It does not read
273	form input or other page-body content. `scripting` (rather than click-scoped
274	`activeTab`) is required because this indexing happens automatically on page
275	load, not from a user click.
276	
277	**`host_permissions: <all_urls>`**
278	Allow two automatic, non-click actions across the tabs the user already has open:
279	(1) capturing the visible tab via `captureVisibleTab` after tab activation, after
280	a page finishes loading, and during a user-requested full refresh, to build
281	thumbnail cards; and (2) running the load-time meta/H1/H2 metadata extractor
282	above. Chrome's click-scoped `activeTab` cannot authorize these automatic
283	background actions, so broad host access is required for the shipped
284	live-thumbnail and auto-indexing behavior. Neither automatic action filters by
285	URL in Meridian's own code; Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` and `scripting` APIs
286	refuse to act on `chrome://`, Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so
287	those are excluded by Chrome's own restrictions, not by a Meridian allowlist.
288	The separate, user-requested full refresh does explicitly skip `chrome://`,
289	`chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's code before switching to
290	them. Meridian makes no network request to a Meridian server.
291	
292	### Optional permissions (requested only on demand)
293	
294	**`bookmarks`** *(optional)*
295	Requested only when the user enables bookmark search in Settings → Local Search
296	or selects the bookmark scope. Used to read bookmark titles, URLs, and folder
297	names to return local-search results. No persistent copy of the bookmark tree is
298	created; denying or revoking it leaves the feature off.
299	
300	**`history`** *(optional)*
301	Requested only when the user enables history search in Settings → Local Search or
302	selects the history scope. Used to read history titles, URLs, and visit times to
303	return local-search results. No persistent history database is created; denying
304	or revoking it leaves the feature off.
305	
306	---

340	## 6. Reconciliation notes
341	
342	Verified against the current source on the "Last updated" date:
343

345	  `unlimitedStorage`, `scripting`, `sidePanel`, `favicon`), optional

374	
375	**Pass — Meridian 1.1.0 is release-ready as the candidate identified below.**
376	
377	Every check that was run is green. The full deterministic repository suite passes

messages.content:
Short answer: it's risky to submit as-is, and here's why.

Chrome Web Store's review process (and its Developer Program Policies) requires your privacy policy to **accurately and specifically disclose what your extension actually does** with user data — not just link to a generic corporate policy. Reviewers (and automated compliance scans) cross-check the policy against:

- the permissions you declare in the manifest
- the data-type disclosures you check in the dashboard's Privacy practices tab
- what the extension is observed doing at runtime

Per `STORE_LISTING.md` §2.4, the current `https://emberstone-studio.com/docs/privacy/` page is **catch-all Emberstone Studio boilerplate**, and it's missing explicit, product-level coverage of things Meridian actually does:

- **Automatic screenshot capture** of visible tabs (`captureVisibleTab`) — sensitive, since it can capture whatever's on screen
- **Automatic per-page content extraction** (meta description + H1/H2 headings) on every page load
- **Automatic tab/browsing-activity collection** (titles, URLs, domains, groups)
- That **preferences sync via the user's own Chrome Sync** (i.e., can travel to their other signed-in devices) — not purely device-local
- That data is **retained persistently** until eviction/tab-close/manual clear — not "session data that deletes automatically" (a phrase generic policies often use, which would be factually wrong here)

If the published policy doesn't mention these, that's a mismatch between disclosed behavior and actual behavior — a common cause of Chrome Web Store rejections or later suspensions, especially since `tabs`, `scripting`, and `host_permissions: <all_urls>` are exactly the kind of "sensitive/broad" permissions Google scrutinizes hardest.

The fix is straightforward: add a Meridian-specific section to that policy page (or a dedicated Meridian policy page) covering the five points above. `STORE_LISTING.md` §3 already has paste-ready language for most of it.

Want me to have the **Writer** draft that policy addendum now, ready for you to publish at the emberstone-studio.com URL before you submit?
Ok, ok. let's write one for meridian, and I'll put it at https://emberstone-studio.com/docs/privacy/meridian

1	# Meridian Privacy Information
2	
3	Last updated: July 26, 2026
4	
5	This document describes the behavior of the Meridian source code in this
6	repository. Meridian is a Chrome extension that runs in the user's browser. The
7	repository does not contain a Meridian-operated backend, analytics SDK,
8	advertising SDK, account system, or telemetry uploader. Chrome itself and the
9	external services listed below may process requests according to their own
10	settings and policies.
11	
12	## Chrome Web Store Limited Use adherence
13	
14	Meridian's use of information received from Chrome APIs adheres to the
15	[Chrome Web Store User Data Policy](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/user-data-faq),
16	including the Limited Use requirements. Specifically, for the source in this
17	repository:
18	
19	- Meridian accesses and processes tab data, page metadata, captured
20	  screenshots, and optional bookmarks/history **only to provide and improve the
21	  user-facing tab-management, local-search, personalization, and thumbnail
22	  features described below**, in response to user actions or automatic in-browser
23	  indexing.
24	- Meridian **does not transfer this data to any Meridian-operated server**; the
25	  repository contains no backend, account system, analytics SDK, advertising
26	  SDK, or telemetry uploader. Data stays in the user's Chrome profile
27	  (`chrome.storage.local`, `chrome.storage.sync`, and IndexedDB) except where the
28	  user's own actions navigate the browser or contact the third-party services
29	  listed under "Remaining network behavior."
30	- Meridian **does not sell** user data, **does not use or transfer it for
31	  advertising, credit-scoring, or lending**, and **does not use it for purposes
32	  unrelated to the extension's single visible purpose**.
33	- Meridian **does not allow humans to read** this data. No human at the
34	  publisher can read tab, metadata, screenshot, bookmark, or history data,
35	  because none of it leaves the user's device to a publisher-controlled system.
36	
37	This statement describes the reviewed source only. The publisher must confirm
38	the same guarantees hold for the exact archive uploaded to the Chrome Web Store
39	and for the answers entered in the store dashboard.
40	
41	## Data the extension accesses
42	
43	| Data | How Meridian uses it | Where it is kept |
44	| --- | --- | --- |
45	| Open tabs and tab groups | Displays, searches, activates, closes, moves, groups, and restores tabs. This includes tab IDs, titles, URLs, domains, group membership, window IDs, and recent activation state. | A search index and workspace/UI state are stored in `chrome.storage.local`. |
46	| Open-page metadata | After an open tab finishes loading, reads its meta description and H1/H2 heading text so local tab search can match page context beyond the title and URL. Meridian does not extract form input or other page-body text. Chrome blocks injection into privileged pages, which remain searchable by the tab data Chrome exposes. | Stored only in that tab's entry in the local search index in `chrome.storage.local`; refreshed after later page loads and removed when the tab closes or extension data is cleared. |
47	| Bookmarks | After the user enables optional bookmark access, displays and searches bookmark titles, URLs, and folder names when the user opens or searches bookmark features. Disabled or ungranted access is not queried. | Results are used in memory; Meridian does not create a persistent copy of the bookmark tree. |
48	| Browser history | After the user enables optional history access, searches history titles, URLs, and visit times when the user opens or searches history features. Disabled or ungranted access is not queried. | Results are used in memory; Meridian does not create a persistent history database. |
49	| Screenshots/thumbnails | Captures the visible contents of active tabs after activation or page load, and during a user-requested full refresh. Automatic captures (after activation or page load) do not check the tab's URL first; Chrome's own `captureVisibleTab` API refuses privileged pages such as `chrome://`, the Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so those attempts fail and store nothing. A user-requested full refresh additionally skips `chrome://`, `chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs before switching to them, so it never focuses those tabs at all. Any other page — including one with sensitive content visible on screen — is captured the same way in both cases. | JPEG blobs are kept in IndexedDB in the extension's local origin; cache metadata and refresh markers are kept in `chrome.storage.local`. Older data-URL entries are migrated into IndexedDB. Storage targets roughly 200 entries and 50 MB, pruning the oldest thumbnails first when over target, but a thumbnail for a tab that is still open is never evicted to make room — actual usage can exceed the target while those tabs stay open. A display/decode error does not delete the stored blob. A tab's thumbnail is removed when that tab closes. |
50	| Workspace and UI state | Stores custom workspace names and tab assignments, tab order, collapsed lanes/sidebar sections, the Meridian tab ID, the previous tab ID, and thumbnail cache metadata. | `chrome.storage.local` in the user's Chrome profile. |
51	| Custom background image | Stores an image selected from the user's device. | IndexedDB in the extension's local origin. Older versions may have left a legacy copy in local extension storage or `localStorage`. |
52	| Preferences | Stores theme, background selection, search provider, enabled local-search sources, new-tab behavior, optional homepage URL, and domain-grouping preference. | `chrome.storage.sync`. Chrome may sync these values through the user's signed-in Chrome profile, subject to the user's Chrome Sync settings. The uploaded custom image bytes and captured thumbnails are not placed in sync storage. |
53	
54	Meridian uses the accessed data to provide its tab-management, search,
55	personalization, and thumbnail features. Repository review found no code that
56	sells this data, uses it for advertising, or uploads it to a
57	Meridian-controlled service. This statement is limited to the reviewed source
58	and is not a verification of any separately published build or store account.
59	
60	## Favicon handling
61	
62	The side panel and tab, bookmark, and history search results pass page URLs only
63	to Chrome's packaged `chrome-extension://.../_favicon/` endpoint to look up
64	icons through the browser's favicon provider. Meridian does not send those URLs
65	or domains to the Google S2 favicon service. If Chrome has no icon or the image
66	cannot load, those surfaces render a generated letter tile from the extension
67	package instead of contacting a third-party fallback.
68	
69	## Remaining network behavior
70	
71	Meridian does not make a background request to its own server, but its UI and
72	user actions can contact external services:
73	
74	- Search-provider icons are loaded from fixed icon URLs at Google,
75	  DuckDuckGo, Bing, and Brave. These fixed requests do not contain a visited
76	  tab, bookmark, or history URL.
77	- New-tab-page cards and their preview can display the `favIconUrl` supplied by
78	  Chrome for an open tab. Depending on Chrome's cache, displaying that URL can
79	  request the icon from the site or the site's chosen icon host; it is not a
80	  Google S2 lookup.
81	- Opening the background settings loads photo thumbnails from
82	  `picsum.photos`. Selecting a Picsum photo loads the chosen full-size image
83	  from that service. The generated photo seed is part of the request URL.
84	- Starting a web search opens a tab at the selected provider (Google,
85	  DuckDuckGo, Bing, or Brave) with the search text in the URL.
86	- Choosing the custom-homepage behavior or opening a tab, bookmark, or history
87	  result navigates Chrome to the selected URL. The destination then receives a
88	  normal browser navigation.
89	- The Settings panel's Emberstone Studio footer shows two outbound links — the
90	  studio site (`https://emberstone-studio.com`) and a Ko-fi donation page
91	  (`https://ko-fi.com/emberstonestudio`). Both are inert until the user
92	  explicitly clicks one, which opens that destination in a new tab. Meridian
93	  performs no background request for them and adds no click tracking or
94	  analytics.
95	- The code fetches the packaged Meridian SVG through
96	  `chrome.runtime.getURL`; that is an extension-local resource, not an Internet
97	  request.
98	
99	External requests above use HTTPS in the current source. The receiving service
100	can observe normal request information such as the user's IP address and
101	browser headers and applies its own privacy policy.
102	
103	## Permissions
104	
105	The manifests request these installed capabilities:
106

  "content": "# Meridian Privacy Information

Last updated: July 26, 2026

Meridian is a Chrome extension that runs entirely in your browser. Meridian has
no Meridian-operated backend, analytics SDK, advertising SDK, account system,
or telemetry uploader. Chrome itself and the external services listed below
may process requests according to their own settings and policies.

## Chrome Web Store Limited Use adherence

Meridian's use of information received from Chrome APIs adheres to the
[Chrome Web Store User Data Policy](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/user-data-faq),
including the Limited Use requirements:

- Meridian accesses and processes tab data, page metadata, captured
  screenshots, and optional bookmarks/history **only to provide and improve the
  user-facing tab-management, local-search, personalization, and thumbnail
  features described below**, in response to user actions or automatic in-browser
  indexing.
- Meridian **does not transfer this data to any Meridian-operated server**;
  Meridian has no backend, account system, analytics SDK, advertising SDK, or
  telemetry uploader. Data stays in your Chrome profile (`chrome.storage.local`,
  `chrome.storage.sync`, and IndexedDB) except where your own actions navigate
  the browser or contact the third-party services listed under "Remaining
  network behavior."
- Meridian **does not sell** user data, **does not use or transfer it for
  advertising, credit-scoring, or lending**, and **does not use it for purposes
  unrelated to the extension's single visible purpose**.
- Meridian **does not allow humans to read** this data. No one at the
  publisher can read tab, metadata, screenshot, bookmark, or history data,
  because none of it leaves your device to a publisher-controlled system.

## Data the extension accesses

| Data | How Meridian uses it | Where it is kept |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open tabs and tab groups | Displays, searches, activates, closes, moves, groups, and restores tabs. This includes tab IDs, titles, URLs, domains, group membership, window IDs, and recent activation state. | A search index and workspace/UI state are stored in `chrome.storage.local`. |
| Open-page metadata | After an open tab finishes loading, reads its meta description and H1/H2 heading text so local tab search can match page context beyond the title and URL. Meridian does not extract form input or other page-body text. Chrome blocks injection into privileged pages, which remain searchable by the tab data Chrome exposes. | Stored only in that tab's entry in the local search index in `chrome.storage.local`; refreshed after later page loads and removed when the tab closes or extension data is cleared. |
| Bookmarks | After you enable optional bookmark access, displays and searches bookmark titles, URLs, and folder names when you open or search bookmark features. Disabled or ungranted access is not queried. | Results are used in memory; Meridian does not create a persistent copy of the bookmark tree. |
| Browser history | After you enable optional history access, searches history titles, URLs, and visit times when you open or search history features. Disabled or ungranted access is not queried. | Results are used in memory; Meridian does not create a persistent history database. |
| Screenshots/thumbnails | Captures the visible contents of active tabs after activation or page load, and during a user-requested full refresh. Automatic captures (after activation or page load) do not check the tab's URL first; Chrome's own `captureVisibleTab` API refuses privileged pages such as `chrome://`, the Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so those attempts fail and store nothing. A user-requested full refresh additionally skips `chrome://`, `chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs before switching to them, so it never focuses those tabs at all. Any other page — including one with sensitive content visible on screen — is captured the same way in both cases. | JPEG blobs are kept in IndexedDB in the extension's local origin; cache metadata and refresh markers are kept in `chrome.storage.local`. Older data-URL entries are migrated into IndexedDB. Storage targets roughly 200 entries and 50 MB, pruning the oldest thumbnails first when over target, but a thumbnail for a tab that is still open is never evicted to make room — actual usage can exceed the target while those tabs stay open. A display/decode error does not delete the stored blob. A tab's thumbnail is removed when that tab closes. |
| Workspace and UI state | Stores custom workspace names and tab assignments, tab order, collapsed lanes/sidebar sections, the Meridian tab ID, the previous tab ID, and thumbnail cache metadata. | `chrome.storage.local` in your Chrome profile. |
| Custom background image | Stores an image you select from your device. | IndexedDB in the extension's local origin. Older versions may have left a legacy copy in local extension storage or `localStorage`. |
| Preferences | Stores theme, background selection, search provider, enabled local-search sources, new-tab behavior, optional homepage URL, and domain-grouping preference. | `chrome.storage.sync`. Chrome may sync these values through your signed-in Chrome profile, subject to your Chrome Sync settings — this means these preferences can travel to your other signed-in devices; it is not Meridian-operated syncing. The uploaded custom image bytes and captured thumbnails are not placed in sync storage. |

Meridian uses the accessed data to provide its tab-management, search,
personalization, and thumbnail features. It does not sell this data, use it
for advertising, or upload it to a Meridian-controlled service.

## Favicon handling

The side panel and tab, bookmark, and history search results pass page URLs only
to Chrome's packaged `chrome-extension://.../_favicon/` endpoint to look up
icons through the browser's favicon provider. Meridian does not send those URLs
or domains to the Google S2 favicon service. If Chrome has no icon or the image
cannot load, those surfaces render a generated letter tile from the extension
package instead of contacting a third-party fallback.

## Remaining network behavior

Meridian does not make a background request to its own server, but its UI and
your actions can contact external services:

- Search-provider icons are loaded from fixed icon URLs at Google,
  DuckDuckGo, Bing, and Brave. These fixed requests do not contain a visited
  tab, bookmark, or history URL.
- New-tab-page cards and their preview can display the `favIconUrl` supplied by
  Chrome for an open tab. Depending on Chrome's cache, displaying that URL can
  request the icon from the site or the site's chosen icon host; it is not a
  Google S2 lookup.
- Opening the background settings loads photo thumbnails from
  `picsum.photos`. Selecting a Picsum photo loads the chosen full-size image
  from that service. The generated photo seed is part of the request URL.
- Starting a web search opens a tab at the selected provider (Google,
  DuckDuckGo, Bing, or Brave) with the search text in the URL.
- Choosing the custom-homepage behavior or opening a tab, bookmark, or history
  result navigates Chrome to the selected URL. The destination then receives a
  normal browser navigation.
- The Settings panel's Emberstone Studio footer shows two outbound links — the
  studio site (`https://emberstone-studio.com`) and a Ko-fi donation page
  (`https://ko-fi.com/emberstonestudio`). Both are inert until you explicitly
  click one, which opens that destination in a new tab. Meridian performs no
  background request for them and adds no click tracking or analytics.
- The code fetches the packaged Meridian SVG through
  `chrome.runtime.getURL`; that is an extension-local resource, not an Internet
  request.

External requests above use HTTPS. The receiving service can observe normal
request information such as your IP address and browser headers and applies
its own privacy policy.

## Permissions

Meridian requests these installed capabilities:

- `tabs` and `tabGroups`: read tab titles and URLs and manage tabs and groups.
- `storage` and `unlimitedStorage`: retain preferences, workspaces, search
  metadata, thumbnails, and custom backgrounds across local storage and
  IndexedDB. Thumbnail data can exceed the
  default storage quota, so `unlimitedStorage` lets the cache hold a useful
  number of entries; Meridian still targets roughly 200 entries / 50 MB and
  prunes the oldest thumbnails first, but never evicts a still-open tab's
  thumbnail, so usage can exceed that target while those tabs stay open.
- `favicon`: use Chrome's packaged favicon provider.
- `sidePanel`: provide the Meridian side-panel UI.
- `scripting`: run the one-shot metadata extractor after an open tab finishes
  loading. This is required because indexing happens automatically rather
  than from a user click; the extractor reads only the page's meta description
  and H1/H2 heading text.
- `<all_urls>` host access: allow automatic visible-tab thumbnail capture after
  activation or page load, a user-requested full refresh, and the one-shot
  metadata extractor after page load. This access is required because
  Chrome's click-scoped `activeTab` permission cannot authorize those automatic
  background actions. Automatic captures and the metadata extractor do not
  filter by URL in Meridian's code; privileged pages (`chrome://`,
  `chrome-extension://`, the Chrome Web Store, other extensions' pages) are
  excluded only because Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` and `scripting` APIs
  refuse to act on them. The user-requested full refresh additionally skips
  `chrome://`, `chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's own code
  before switching to them.

`bookmarks` and `history` are optional permissions. Chrome prompts only when
you enable the matching Local Search setting or select that search scope.
Denial leaves the source off. Disabling the setting removes the grant, and
revocation through Chrome also turns off the saved source and prevents further
queries.

Chrome blocks extension access to some privileged pages. Meridian catches those
access failures and leaves the unavailable tab details or thumbnail empty.

## Retention and control

Most persistent data remains inside the extension's local or sync storage until
it is replaced, evicted, manually cleared, or removed during extension or
profile cleanup — it is not session data that deletes automatically. Bookmark
and history queries do not create a separate persistent copy. Closing a tab
requests deletion of its cached thumbnail and tab-search entry, including
extracted metadata. You can also clear extension data through Chrome's
site/extension data controls. Bookmark and history access can be removed from
Meridian's Local Search settings or Chrome's extension controls.

## References

- [Chrome's Manifest V3 favicon endpoint](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/how-to/ui/favicons)
- [Chrome Web Store program policies](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/policies)
- [Chrome Web Store user data FAQ](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/user-data-faq)

Which do you want?

Not really — this is a hard Chrome platform constraint, not something fixable in Meridian's code.

When an extension overrides the new tab page via `chrome_url_overrides.newtab`, Chrome **deliberately** shows the full `chrome-extension://<id>/page.html` URL in the omnibox instead of hiding it or showing something friendlier like `chrome://newtab`. This is intentional — it's a transparency/security measure so users can always tell their new tab page has been replaced by a third-party extension (and can quickly see which one, via the ID). There's no manifest key, custom protocol, or supported workaround to shorten or rebrand that URL — even the "New Tab Override" style extensions on the Chrome Web Store all show the same raw `chrome-extension://` URL.

The extension ID itself (`kilmpmjaecbplakbckcgaocoknfegamk`) is also not something you control — it's derived from your Web Store listing/key, not a name you can pick to look nicer.

The only real lever you have is the **tab title** (`<title>` in `meridian.html`) and the **favicon**, which do show in the tab strip — those are already branded as "Meridian." The omnibox text itself is Chrome's call, not the extension's.

Sources: [Chrome Web Store — chrome_url_overrides (MDN)](https://developer.mozilla.org/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/chrome_url_overrides), [Chromium issue: omnibox not highlighted on new tab override](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41345068)
